answer: Identity-bond decay blocks fake identities. An agent anchors one identity by locking a bond worth twice its 30-day earnings. One cipher key signs all its work, so a bond cannot be copied across accounts. The bond decays over a 20-epoch horizon, and honest use renews only a little. Making 100 fakes costs 100 bonds, about 200 times one month's earnings, more than those fakes could split. An honest agent pays once and earns undiluted rewards.
